about: Strip contract of mission ams at 40 px (docs/design/ams40.md, rules "replaced correctly"). Generated by tools/art40/contract/extract.ts: do not edit by hand.

telegraph.name: Telegraph (no reference class; length = the tele ticks)

held.name: Held pose (no reference class; the code holds it)

reaction.name: Reaction loop (cower, panic; nearest class: idle fidget)

turn.name: Turn / transition (code-driven squash or in-between; count read by code)

mechanical.name: Mechanical / rigid part (keeps its mechanical count)

prop.name: Prop or effect of the strip (bind, ticket, cork, flash, debris)

aim.name: Aim pose (frames indexed by the aim step; count = the aim steps)

overlay.name: Front overlay (drawn with its body strip’s frame index: same count)

piece.name: Piece of a composed boss rig (frames indexed by role in the code)

roles.name: Frame roles picked by code (each frame one pose; count = the roles)

ui.name: UI picture (out of scope: select panels, portraits)

other.name: Unclassed (decide per strip; log the reason)

notes: The heroes, the Swan, the handhaver and the delivery rider also appear in oldenzaal and oat: shared ids change everywhere (plan "Scope"; intended).

Animator rule: a strip’s `durations` override any ticksPerFrame the code passes (Animator.play). The hero run strip has none today (the code plays it at 3 ticks per frame); a baked strip always has durations (src/engine/baked.ts), so the baked run keeps 36 ticks per cycle (logicTicks) and the TUNING knob no longer changes it. The hero knife / throw strips have durations, which win over the computed speed.
Turn strips are drawn by code (Turner, RIDER_TURN, PERSON_TURN_TICKS, HOSTAGE_TURN_TICKS): their counts are code numbers.

characters.name: handhaver (city enforcement officer) and the BOETE ticket

variants.variant: skin a (base)
skin b: a second HumanStyle (skinB, hairA) rendered separately, not a runtime recolour
skin c: a third HumanStyle (skinC, hairA, hairStyle curly: a PART change, not only palette)
the thrown ticket (prop, centre anchor)

rules.text: Death strip by damage kind (knife, explosion, fire, crush, else die; missing → die). Played once; the corpse timer starts when the strip is done, so its total ticks set how long the body lies (cosmetic, but sims see removal ticks).
Reaction strips by name (photo → photo-pose, gloat, cower → cower, else panic, else idle). Every enemy answers photo, gloat and cower.
A blast death launches the body (vx ±1.5, vy −3.0) while the strip plays: the strip must read as airborne for its first frames.
The Turner draws `turn` frames 0,1 narrowing, flips, then 1,0 widening (2 widths × 2 ticks = 8 ticks): the strip must keep exactly 2 frames (Turner widths = 2) or the Turner call changes with it.
Skin picked at spawn: param skin a|b|c, else rng 0..2; a → enemy/handhaver, b/c → enemy/handhaver-<skin>.
Body 14 × 30 (Enemy opts w 14, h 30); hp 20, score 300.

Walks at 0.6 px/tick; the walk strip plays 8 frames × 6 ticks (HANDHAVER_WALK_TPF) = 48 ticks per cycle at the nominal speed → 28.8 px per cycle (two steps of 14.4 px). The Animator rate is strideRate(vx, 0.6) (clamped 0.5–1.6).
Tell: durations [8, 8, 9999] (the last frame held); the telegraph lasts tele 24 ticks (difficulty-scaled) before the ticket leaves.

Throw: the ticket spawns on the tick the throw strip starts (frame 0 = the flick in the code); throw mode lasts throwTicks 8, then recover 40 ticks, where the throw strip finishes (HANDHAVER_THROW_TIMING [3,5,4,4,4] = 20 ticks) and idle plays.
The ticket leaves from x + facing × 10, y − chestY 25 (code numbers, no frame point); handInView tests x + facing × 8. The hand in the art should meet that place on the release frame.

GLOAT_FRAME = { write 0, write2 1, tear 2, drop 3, done 4 }: the game sets anim.index per phase (write 48 ticks alternating 0/1 every 8, tear 12, drop 14, then done). The strip needs ≥ 5 frames with these roles or the constant moves with it (rule 4: exported names).
The torn page drops from x + facing × 9, y − 32 (code numbers): the raised hand of the drop frame should be there.
Cower loops at HANDHAVER_COWER_TPF 3 (deferred strip).

The scan car boss draws its fleeing driver with enemy/handhaver/walk: frame = floor(tick / 3) % frameCount (driverFrames read once from getFrames(ID.driverRun).length). A new count works; a slower look needs the 3-tick step changed.
Spawned by the mayor boss (adds every 420 ticks) and by mission oat (sections a–e) and the ring crew (dormant) reuses HANDHAVER_STYLE: shared ids change everywhere (intended, plan "Scope").
enemy/boete-ticket/fly: the thrown ticket (8 × 5 box, ticksPerFrame 4, look anim) and the death tumble (3 tickets); also the oat budget fines (src/game/budget/pay.ts).
ams-d: prewarmed with the mayor arena (section-d.ts prewarm).

keep: ids enemy/handhaver[-b|-c]/<strip> and enemy/boete-ticket/fly
turn = 2 frames (Turner widths 2, 2 ticks each)
gloat ≥ 5 frames with the GLOAT_FRAME roles (or export the new indices)
throw: release on frame 0 (ticket spawns at strip start); throw+recover logic 8 + 40 ticks
walk: 28.8 px per cycle at 0.6 px/tick (or a new tpf that keeps the stride on the floor)
points hand, head, hip on every frame; the release hand near (10, −25)
skin c keeps curly hair (a part, not only palette)

rules.text: The run torso is drawn at legs.index % torso frame count: the torso run count must equal (or divide) the legs run count (12 today).

The torso starts AT the release frame (the bomb leaves at once; the wind-up frames before it are never shown in play). The code passes tpf = floor(throwTicks 12 / (n − release)) but the strip durations win: today [5, 4, 3, 3, 3, 5], 14 ticks from the release, the action 12.

PHYSICS: bullets leave from hip + frame 0 `muzzle` of the aim strip (shoot, shoot-up, shoot-down, shoot-diag-*); fallback muzzles in TUNING when missing. Frame 0 of every shoot strip must carry the muzzle at the barrel tip.
PHYSICS: the torso joins at the legs frame `hip` (also the muzzle / hand base). Every legs frame needs `hip`.
Crouch transitions are draw-only: onceFrame(tr, stripTicks(tr) − crouchT) and the torso sits on that frame’s hip.

Swan rider poses: drawn with their hip on the Swan `seat` point; frame = the Swan’s pick (run 0/1, glide/squat/flap f & 1, paddle-up) or stripFrame on world.tick. Missing → ride-sit → mount frame 1 at +17 px. 2-frame poses are read as 0/1 by the Swan (pickRiderFrame).

Seated in vehicles: mount frame floor(tick / 16) (drawSeated); mount frame 1 is the ride fallback with its hip at (0, −17) (MOUNT_HIP_DROP).

The snore fx sits at the full frame’s `head` point.
